content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (negative sentiment < -0.5) — model fails to capture sharp declines, especially after recent spikes.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often holds high prices for 2–3 days before correcting — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day of lag.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility; true price often reverts to 10–15-day moving average within 3–5 days of extreme deviation.
- Overshoot after spikes: if price spikes > +5% from 10-day average, model forecasts 10–15% higher than true outcome — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods — reduce forecast by 1–3% for each day beyond 10-day horizon if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
